advances: Ordinary normalized depth and affine simplex distance along a signed equal-volume shape path, with a separate actual mixed compatibility realization.

proof:
Write $e=\varepsilon^d$. The original deletion is $\varepsilon T$ up to its boundary. Scaling restores $|\widetilde K|=(1-e)\alpha^dV=V$, and $\alpha\varepsilon<1$ in the volume-restored range. Thus the removed part relative to $T$ is $\alpha\varepsilon T$ and the added part is $\alpha T\setminus T$, both of volume $\delta V$. This gives the signed identity, total variation and symmetric difference. The halfspace $\{\sum_i x_i\ge1\}$ realizes the maximal discrepancy. The first moment of the deleted corner before dilation is $\varepsilon^{d+1}Vg$, proving the centroid formula. Since $\alpha=(1+\delta)^{1/d}\le1+\delta/d$ and $\alpha<2$, the centroid scaling factor lies between one and $1+(2+1/d)\delta$. Each coordinate of $g$ is $1/(d+1)$, giving the claimed shift.

The canonical centroid caps of $T$ each have volume $\Gamma_dV$ by homothety and cover the whole space because the barycentric coordinates sum to one. Since $K_\varepsilon\subset T$, these same caps bound every point's normalized depth by $\Gamma_d/(1-e)$. Depth is unchanged by dilation. The $2d$ points $e_i,\varepsilon e_i$ are exposed vertices: $x_i$ exposes the first, and $x_i-2\sum_j x_j$ exposes the second. Thus the body is no simplex for $d\ge2$, and accepted ordinary rigidity ea91e021ff1f4416 gives the strict lower bound.

Suppose $0<\varepsilon\le1/d$ and $\rho=d_{H,\infty}(K_\varepsilon,S)<c_d\varepsilon$. Every $p\in S$ has $p_i\ge-\rho$ and $\varepsilon-d\rho\le\sum_jp_j\le1+d\rho$. The proximity of $e_i$ forces a vertex $p^i$ of $S$ with $p^i_i\ge1-\rho$. Then $|p^i_i-1|\le\rho$, and for $j\ne i$ the sum bound and the other coordinate lower bounds give $-\rho\le p^i_j\le(2d-1)\rho$. These vertices are distinct because $2d\rho<1$. Put $f_i(x)=x_i-2\sum_jx_j$, of dual norm $2d-1$. Its maximum on $K_\varepsilon$ is $-\varepsilon$. On each assigned vertex $p^j$ it is at most $-1+(2d-1)^2\rho<-\varepsilon-(2d-1)\rho$, since $c_d\varepsilon\le(1-\varepsilon)/(2d(2d-1))$. Yet the support comparison gives $\max_S f_i\ge-\varepsilon-(2d-1)\rho$. There is at most one unassigned vertex, so there must be one, $p^0$, at which all these maxima occur. Writing $P=\sum_jp^0_j$, summing the required bounds gives $P\le d\varepsilon/(2d-1)+d\rho$. Together with $P\ge\varepsilon-d\rho$ this forces $\rho\ge c_d\varepsilon$, a contradiction.

For the comparison with $T$, a point of coordinate sum $s<\varepsilon$ is moved to $K_\varepsilon$ by adding $(\varepsilon-s)/d$ to each coordinate, and the origin requires distance $\varepsilon/d$. Scaling gives the two orbit bounds. The equal-volume comparison with $T$ costs at most $\alpha\varepsilon/d+(\alpha-1)\le4\varepsilon/d$, using $\alpha<2$ and $\delta\le2\varepsilon^d$. For a simplex sandwich of $K_\varepsilon$, the inside simplex has infinity diameter at most one, so the distance to it is at most $\lambda-1$. The lower bound follows. The centroid homothet $S=g+a(T-g)$ with $a=1-(d+1)\varepsilon/d$ has minimal coordinate sum $\varepsilon$ and lies in $K_\varepsilon$. The dilation of $S$ about $g$ by $1/a$ contains $K_\varepsilon$, giving the upper bound since $a\ge1/2$. Affine invariance transports this to $\widetilde K$.

For centroid matching let $v=g-g_{\widetilde K}$. Compare $\widetilde K+v$ first to $T+v$, which costs at most $\delta$. For $T$ versus $T+v$, a halfspace normal scaled to infinity norm one sees a threshold difference at most $d\lVert v\rVert_\infty$. Slice along a coordinate of normal magnitude one. The other coordinates lie in $[0,1]^{d-1}$, so the volume change is at most the threshold difference. Divide by $V$ to obtain the stated discrepancy. Depth and the two shape distances are invariant under this translation. Each orbit-distance lower bound is a positive constant times $\varepsilon$, while $\delta=O_d(\varepsilon^d)$, proving the limits.

Finally every point of $A$ has positive coordinates and sum between $d/[2(d+1)]$ and $(2d+1)/[2(d+1)]$. These bounds lie strictly between $\alpha\varepsilon$ and $\alpha$, since $\alpha<2\le d$. Thus $A$ is strictly contained in $\widetilde K$. At either exposed endpoint the hull has exactly its given fiber. At the middle base the two endpoint weights agree, so their continuous contribution is a scalar multiple of a point of $A$. Convex combinations with the middle body stay in $\widetilde K$, and the entire middle body is present. The three bases exhaust the integer points of the projection and the hull has interior because it has a positive middle fiber and extends to both sides.
statement:
For $d\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/[2(d+1)]$, put $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $V=|T|=1/d!$, $K_\varepsilon=T\cap\{\sum_i x_i\ge\varepsilon\}$, $\alpha=(1-\varepsilon^d)^{-1/d}$, $\widetilde K=\alpha K_\varepsilon$, and $\delta=\varepsilon^d/(1-\varepsilon^d)$. Then $|\widetilde K|=V$ and for every measurable $E$ its normalized signed mass difference from $T$ is $[|E\cap(\alpha T\setminus T)|-|E\cap\alpha\varepsilon T|]/V$. Each part has volume $\delta V$. The normalized symmetric difference is $2\delta$, total variation and maximal closed-halfspace discrepancy are both $\delta$, and the centroid is $\alpha(1-\varepsilon^{d+1})g/(1-\varepsilon^d)$, where $g$ is the centroid of $T$. Its displacement from $g$ is coordinatewise nonnegative and has infinity norm at most $\delta$.

For the volume-preserving truncation $\widetilde K$ just defined, its maximal normalized ordinary depth $D$ satisfies $0<D(\widetilde K)-\Gamma_d\le\Gamma_d\delta$. Let $c_d=(d-1)/[2d(2d-1)]$. For all $0<\varepsilon\le1/d$ the unscaled truncation $K_\varepsilon$ satisfies $d_{H,\infty}(K_\varepsilon,S)\ge c_d\varepsilon$ for every simplex $S$, including degenerate ones, and $d_{H,\infty}(K_\varepsilon,T)=\varepsilon/d$. Consequently, in the volume-restored range,
$$
\alpha c_d\varepsilon\le\inf_S d_{H,\infty}(\widetilde K,S)\le\alpha\varepsilon/d.
$$
The upper bound with volume-$V$ comparison simplices is $4\varepsilon/d$. For the affine-invariant factor $b(K)=\inf\{\lambda\ge1:S\subseteq K\subseteq p+\lambda(S-p),\ S\text{ a simplex},\ p\in S\}$,
$$
c_d\varepsilon\le b(\widetilde K)-1\le2(d+1)\varepsilon/d.
$$
Translating $\widetilde K$ to match $g$ preserves these depth and shape distances and gives cap discrepancy at most $(1+d\,d!)\delta$ from $T$. For each exponent $0<s<d$, the depth excess divided by either simplex-orbit distance to power $s$ tends to zero as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

The actual hull of the lifts of $A=g+(T-g)/2$ at $-1,1$ and $\widetilde K$ at $0$ has exactly these three positive full-dimensional integer fibers throughout the stated volume-restored range. Each endpoint has volume $2^{-d}V$, and $A\subset\operatorname{int}\widetilde K$.
title: Volume-preserving simplex truncation obstructs low-order shape coercivity
